summary: A listed company wants to change its name and must meet specific conditions regarding time, revenue, or investment. It needs to prove these conditions are met through a chartered accountant certificate when asking shareholders for approval. The company must also apply to the Registrar of Companies and follow the Companies Act rules.
points: Must wait at least one year from its last name change before changing its name again
Must earn at least fifty percent of its total revenue in the past year from the new activity shown by the new name
Must invest at least fifty percent of its total assets into the new activity or project
Must change its name within six months if it changes its business activities without updating its name
Must file an application for name availability with the Registrar of Companies
Must include a practicing chartered accountant certificate in the notice for shareholders' approval
example: Sunrise Papers Limited decided to change its primary business to software development and wants a new name to match. The company checked the rules to ensure it qualifies. First, it has been two years since its last name change. Second, the company invested sixty percent of its total assets into the new software project, which satisfies the investment condition. Before asking the shareholders to vote on the new name, Sunrise Papers Limited obtained a certificate from a practicing chartered accountant confirming that the fifty percent asset condition was met. Finally, the company applied to the Registrar of Companies for name availability and prepared the notice for its shareholders with the required certificate attached.

terms.meaning: a company whose securities are traded on a stock exchange
the sum of fixed assets, advances, works in progress, inventories, investments, trade receivables, and cash equivalents
an office that deals with the administration of companies under the law
a certified professional accountant who checks and verifies financial records

watch: A company cannot rely on revenue alone if it has not waited one year, but it can choose to meet either the revenue condition or the asset condition.
